title: Berlin Altbau - Quick Summary
kicker: WALK OF BERLIN • LIVING IN BERLIN
items: **On paper, Altbau means two Mietspiegel bands:** flats first ready to move into until 1918, and from 1919 to 1949.
**The band decides your line in the rent index**, together with floor area and residential location.
**A side wing and a back house** almost always mean a building from before 1914; the 1925 code stopped new back buildings for flats.
**Courtyards were sized for a fire engine:** 5.34 by 5.34 metres under the 1853 code, at least 60 square metres from 1887.
**A plain front can hide an old house.** Berlin stripped stucco in waves, most of all in the 1950s.
**A Berliner Zimmer**, the corner room with one window onto the courtyard, points to a building from before 1914.
**Trust the courtyard and floor plan over the facade** when the clues disagree.
**Confirm the year** in the Denkmaldatenbank, the city's building-age map or the building file.
